contexts.text: He who knows how to think well, has no need to learn to think from what is artificial...

Hewn stones, and those upon which the iron has been moved signified things artificial, and thus counterfeit things of worship; that is, what are from the proprium, or from a production of the heart of man; which was to prophane worship.
The speech of good Spirits, and of angelic Spirits... in choirs, has often been heard by me... no words, or ideas flow in... to which there adheres anything artificial...
Evil Spirits can also, by their artifices, produce heat...
There are some in the world who act by means of artifices and lies, whence come evils... the means (they make use of) are deceits, lies, and artifices. Such relate to the sores called tubercles...
(The inhabitants of Jupiter) do not care for things artificial.
(Thus the formation again of artificial Heavens is guarded against.)
There are (in Heaven)... handicrafts and works. TCR 694:3.
That artificial things, relatively to natural ones, are of no value. SE 252, Explained.
False miracles are those which are contrived by evil Spirits, or Devils, by artificial methods...
Evil Spirits study nothing more than... to imitate those things which are of Heaven, in order by imitations and artifices to make game of minds...
That the delights and deliciousnesses produced by evil Spirits are like the artificial things in the world [made of] colours and wax.
I was shown by means of a choir, who wanted to celebrate the Lord by means of representations, and I perceived that it was from themselves, thus artificial...
That good is turned into evil and truth into falsity, in the World of Spirits, from deceit, from art, or from nature. SEIndex1 65. Artificial.
Whatever is done artificially, closes the way towards interior things. Explained.
Bread cut with a knife is that which counterfeits what is celestial... as everything done artificially...
(On a Spirit who was delighted with artifices for their own sake.)
Aristotle said that he is a fool who wishes to think from what is artificial, for these things are seen from thought, not thought from things artificial.

There was one whom I supposed to be a good Christian, because he was in natural good, and did his work eagerly; he was also good-natured, and at the same time very ingenious in his handicraft, but I observed that he would not have been of that character if he could have helped it...

The evil turn that (sphere) to themselves, with every artifice of dominion... but the good make use of no artifice, but simply say that that is not good, and do not add artifices, or inspire desires and pleasures, as the evil do.
